newsitem.title: USA: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Pluma, Ramco, Total Control rise.
newsitem.headline: IPO HIGHLIGHTS - Pluma, Ramco, Total Control rise.

text.p: Wall Street investment bankers raised roughly $141.2 million on Tuesday in three initial public offerings, with all three stocks posting gains at midday.

Ramco Energy Plc sold five million American Depositary shares for $17.60 each. The ADSs were trading at $17.75 on a "when issued" basis on the American Stock Exchange. The British energy services and exploration company plans to use some of the funds to develop projects in the Caspian region.

Pluma Inc rose 3/4 to 12-3/4 after its debut on the New York Stock Exchange. The North Carolina company manufactures fleece and jersey active wear and sells products to companies including Adidas AG, Nike Inc and Walt Disney Co.

Of the 3.1 million shares of Pluma offered, 2.5 million were sold by the company and 600,000 were offered by selling shareholders. The shares priced at $12, the low end of their IPO price range of $12 to $14.
J.P. Morgan & Co was the lead underwriter of both Pluma and Ramco Energy.
Total Control Products Inc also posted a moderate premium on its first day of trading, rising 1/2 to 8-1/2.

The two million shares priced at $8, the low end of their estimated pricing range of $8 to $10. The company also cut back the number of shares offered from an original estimate of 2.75 million, according to a regulatory filing.

The Melrose Park, Illinois company sold 1.65 million shares in the offering with the remainder sold by shareholders. Total Control develops technology used to control automated industrial equipment, such as the machinery used on factory floors.
